description: The three canonical ledgers holon-knowledge/ledger/executions.jsonl, intents.jsonl and plans.jsonl are not in created_at order on main: measured about 13 adjacent rows out of order in executions, 3 in intents and 3 in plans, and executions mixes the 'Z' and '+00:00' timestamp styles, which sort differently as strings. Merges that append one side's rows after the other's cause the disorder. When a conflict is resolved by interleaving rows by created_at, existing rows move, so a merge shows hundreds of removed and added ledger lines although no row changed, and every other open pull request touching the ledgers conflicts over the moved lines. The one-time reorder is an explicit, maintainer-authorised exception to the append-only ledger rule.
goal: 1) Add one small new script scripts/normalise_ledgers.py (with a pure function importable by tests) that sorts a ledger by created_at parsed as a UTC datetime (not as a string), with a stable tie-break on the existing row order, and rewrites every created_at to the canonical 'Z' form, without changing any other field; then run it once so the three canonical ledgers on main are sorted and canonical. The set of rows must be identical before and after, proved by a test that compares parsed rows (row multiset equal, only order and the created_at spelling differ). 2) Make the conflict reconcilers (flow/ledger_reconcile.py, flow/ledger_interleave.py, ledger/reconcile.py) produce a merge that keeps the base's rows in their existing positions and only inserts the incoming rows, so a merge of a sorted base is additions only and never moves or removes an existing row. 3) Add a check (in the new script, with a --check mode and a test) that fails when a ledger is not in created_at order or holds a non-canonical created_at. Writers of rows spread across the review modules are out of scope and stay untouched. Module line budgets are frozen: do not edit holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json or any budget-check script; put new logic in new small modules where a touched module has no headroom, and keep every touched module within its current budget.
rationale: As long as the base ledgers are unsorted, the rule to interleave by created_at and the rule that ledgers are append-only contradict each other, and every ledger conflict resolution rewrites hundreds of existing lines and conflicts with every other open pull request.
acceptance_criteria: After the change each of the three canonical ledgers is in non-decreasing created_at order when parsed as UTC datetimes, and every created_at ends in 'Z'.
A test proves the set of rows is identical before and after normalisation: same parsed rows, only order and the created_at spelling differ; no row is added, lost or altered otherwise.
Merging incoming rows into a sorted base through each reconciler keeps every base row at its position and only inserts the incoming rows; a test fails on the old behaviour that moves base rows.
The check mode exits non-zero for an unsorted ledger or a '+00:00' timestamp and zero for the normalised ledgers.
No writer of ledger rows outside the three reconcilers is changed, and no other source file changes.
The module budgets file and every budget-check script are untouched and every touched module stays within its current line budget.
uv run pytest passes for the new and the existing ledger reconcile and interleave tests.
